drug_class: PARP inhibitor (a type of targeted cancer therapy)
purpose: Rucaparib is used to treat certain types of ovarian, fallopian tube, or peritoneal cancer in adults who have a specific genetic mutation called BRCA. It is used either after other treatments have been tried or as maintenance therapy to help keep cancer from coming back. Your doctor will test your tumor or blood to see if this medicine is right for you.
how_it_works: Cancer cells sometimes rely on a repair system in the body to survive and keep growing. Rucaparib blocks a protein called PARP, which cancer cells use to fix their damaged DNA. Without this repair tool, the cancer cells cannot survive and they die off, helping to slow or stop the cancer from growing.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, and upset stomach are very common. You may also feel very tired or weak. Other common side effects include loss of appetite, constipation or diarrhea, anemia (low red blood cell counts which can make you feel more tired), and elevated liver enzyme levels seen on blood tests. Some people notice changes in taste.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious decreases in your blood cell counts, which raises your risk of infection, bleeding, or severe anemia — your doctor will monitor your blood regularly. There is a small but serious risk of developing a secondary blood cancer such as leukemia or a bone marrow problem called myelodysplastic syndrome. Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, as it can harm an unborn baby. Use reliable birth control during treatment and for some time after stopping. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as interactions are possible.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 600 mg (two 300 mg tablets) taken by mouth twice a day, approximately 12 hours apart. You can take it with or without food. Try to take it at the same times every day. If you miss a dose, skip it and take the next dose at your regular time — do not double up. Swallow the tablets whole.
